page: Microsoft Azure D8d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. In addition to compute and RAM, it includes 322 GB of fast local SSD storage intended for caching and temporary scratch operations. No discrete GPU acceleration is included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations position the D8d_v5 primarily within the median performance bracket for general compute workloads. The system achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6177.0 and a single-core score of 1653.0, corroborated by a PassMark CPU score of 11469.91 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 7759.55. System memory demonstrates consistent uncached read throughput of 60.04 GB/sec and write throughput of 41.67 GB/sec. CPU instruction capabilities include AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, maintaining steady instruction efficiency. However, parallel compression tests indicate limited scaling, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registering at 32.04 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile of comparative benchmarks.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the inclusion of direct-attached local SSD storage offers lower input/output latency for ephemeral data without requiring extra provisioned volumes. With measured static web serving reaching 12.33 GB/sec and Redis key-value operations executing at 8.08 million per second, the server delivers stable density for medium-scale enterprise tasks. Suitable workloads include production web serving, relational database instances, continuous integration runners, and general backend application environments.
